newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-US experts eye CPI, retail data Sept 9 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-US experts eye CPI, retail data Sept 9 wk.

text.p: Reports on inflation and retail sales will offer conflicting views of the U.S. economy when they are released next week, said U.S. economists in a Reuters survey.

"The (Treasury) market is going to look at CPI (Consumer Price Index) and PPI (Producer Price Index) to see whether there is any inflation pressure, but the real important numbers are retail sales," said John Williams, managing director at BT Securities Corp.

On average, 26 economists forecast August retail sales jumped 0.7 percent, compared to July's 0.1 percent increase. Excluding automobiles, retail sales are expected to climb 0.4 percent, up from a 0.3-percent rise last month.
The experts said they would use the retail sales report to gauge whether consumer demand has slipped since July.
"It will tell us how much the consumer floats from his second-quarter pace," Williams said.
Languid consumer demand would help slow economic growth and keep inflation under control, he said.
Survey respondents said next week's price data will be a secondary focus because it gauges only past inflation.
Steve Ricchiuto, chief financial economist at BZW Securities Inc, said investors will eye CPI for indications of the Federal Reserve's next move.

On average, the experts forecast CPI rose 0.2 percent in August after a 0.3-percent rise in July. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, is expected to be up 0.2 percent, they said.
"If we get a surprisingly favorable CPI number, it's going to take (away) a lot of the sting that the Fed will tighten in September," said Ricchiuto.
The Commerce Department is scheduled to release both the CPI and retail sales on Friday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
